blocks.value: Storage comes in two kinds. Volatile storage (like RAM) is temporary and loses its contents when the computer loses power; a variable in a running Java program lives here. Non-volatile storage (like a disk) is permanent; a saved file lives here.

A computer file is a collection of data stored on a non-volatile device. Files come in two categories: a text file holds data encoded as readable text (using a scheme like ASCII or Unicode), while a binary file holds data that isn't text-encoded and can't be read in a text editor, like images or compiled .class files.

Files are organized into folders (directories). The full drive plus the chain of directories leading to a file is its path, for example C:\Java\Chapter8\example.txt. On Windows, the backslash (\) separates path components.
An absolute path is complete on its own and needs no other information to find a file. A relative path depends on other context, like the current working directory, to be resolved.
